seen_animation: Grey line scenery (wave lines, a slanted stick at top left, a low curved bank at the bottom) stays fixed. In frame 1 a black-line dolphin is at the right edge, tilted about 45 degrees with its snout low and to the left and its dorsal fin pointing up and right; its rear is cut off by the frame edge. Through frames 2-8 the body rotates toward horizontal while staying at the right edge, and more of the body comes into view. By frames 9-10 it is level, facing left, and the forked tail is visible at the right. In frames 11-16 the level dolphin glides steadily left and slightly upward, ending about two thirds of the way across, in the upper third of the frame.
seen_film: Over rippling grey water, a pale white animal shape enters at the right edge in frame 1, angled diagonally with its bright end high at the right and its body trailing down to the left. Through frames 2-8 the shape flattens toward horizontal while it stays near the right edge. From frames 9-16 it swims level toward the left and slightly upward, ending about two thirds of the way across, in the upper third of the frame.
named_subject: a dolphin (the c.png dolphin doodle, mirrored to face left), standing in for the pale swimming animal in the film
evidence: a.png 1-4 vs d.png 1-4: both show the figure at the right edge on a steep diagonal, partly cut off. a.png 5-8 vs d.png 5-8: both flatten toward horizontal at the same height while staying at the right edge. a.png 9-16 vs d.png 9-16: both travel left and slightly up at the same rate and height; in a.png 16 and d.png 16 the figure spans roughly x 1335-1465 at the same vertical band. In e.png/f.png the per-frame leftward step in frames 21-26 is close to the film's (about 190-220 px per 8-panel row step, matching). g.png shows one continuous right-to-left path with evenly growing spacing and no reversals or gaps. Consecutive e.png frames 1-26 show no doubling, redraw or size pop; the figure keeps the same stroke set throughout.
primary_gap: In e.png frames 1-8 the dolphin is tilted steeply and clipped so that only the snout, fin and a fragment of the flipper read, which makes the early frames look like a hooked shape rather than a dolphin rising out of the water as clearly as the film's diagonal body does.
closes_when: In e.png frames 1-8 a larger part of the body outline (belly line toward the tail) is visible inside the frame edge so the dolphin is recognizable from the first frame while keeping the same diagonal angle and position.
protect: The matched timing and placement (diagonal entry at right edge, flattening by frames 8-9 of e.png, steady leftward-upward glide to the same end point); the doodle's open, gapped single strokes, the hooked dorsal fin crossing the body line, the short flipper ticks and forked tail; the fixed grey scenery; the absence of size changes or redraws between frames.
identity_gap: The character is the c.png dolphin mirrored to face left with its construction and stroke gaps kept; only the early clipped frames make it briefly hard to recognize.
